claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a homogeneous high-temperature BCC structure.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between a modest thermodynamic drive toward phase separation or ordering and kinetic hindrance.
Al-induced local lattice distortions kinetically hinder phase transformation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The Al content lowers the thermodynamic driving force for immediate phase separation at high temperature.
The Al content increases diffusion activation barriers in the alloy.
Rapid cooling retains the high-temperature BCC state.
Slow cooling permits nucleation and growth of secondary phases driven by thermodynamic instability.
The high-temperature BCC stability regime occurs above approximately 1100 K.
The relevant lower-temperature transformation regime extends below approximately 700 K.
Local compositional fluctuations induced by Al contribute to the activation barrier for atomic rearrangement.
At high temperature, the driving force for transformation is low.
At high temperature, diffusion is rapid enough to maintain the BCC arrangement.
As temperature decreases, thermodynamic instability increases and favors phase separation or ordering.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain a uniform, single-phase BCC microstructure.
Slowly cooled samples will develop secondary phases, ordered structures, or precipitates.
Rapid solidification from the melt produces a metastable single-phase BCC baseline in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
At temperatures well above the proposed predictive window, BCC is inherently stable regardless of cooling rate.
At temperatures well below the proposed predictive window, transformation becomes complete regardless of cooling rate.
The critical cooling rate and transformation temperatures have not yet been determined.
Small compositional fluctuations may alter the balance between thermodynamic driving force and kinetic barriers.
